'''Les Pages Jèrriaises''' ([[English language|English]]: ''The Jèrriais Pages'') is a collection of thousands of pages in and about [[Jèrriais]] posted on the internet. It was created and is maintained by [[Geraint Jennings]]. It is the largest collection of [[Norman language|Norman]] materials on the internet. It has also been praised in Normandy as an example of how a Norman dialect has managed to modernise itself.<ref>''Presse de la Manche'' 10/6/2001</ref> Les Pages Jèrriaises have also featured prominently in a national newspaper.<ref>''Jersey Evening Post'' 22/4/2000.</ref>

Les Pages Jèrriaises are divided into sections containing vocabulary (usually with English, and sometimes French, translation), grammar, authors, poems, songs, texts, and articles, information on [[Jersey]] and its parishes, a [[FAQ]], an introduction to Jèrriais, and quizzes and games, all in Jèrriais. It contains a repository of old Jèrriais texts (such as poems, stories, and articles), published and made available to the general public.<ref>''Jersey Evening Post'' 18/5/1999</ref>

Les Pages Jèrriaises are sometimes used as a supplement to Jèrriais teaching material in classrooms on Jersey, and is also used as a resource by Jèrriais learners abroad, as well as to connect Jèrriais speakers who have left the island.<ref>''Independent on Sunday'' 2/4/2000</ref> They have been used as a source for Jèrriais-related research by individuals outside of Jersey, including [[Tony Le Sauteur]]'s pages on the history of Jèrriais in [[Quebec]].<ref>[http://tonylesauteur.com/arbre8.htm "La bouonne vielle langue jèrriaise au Tchubec!"]</ref>

== History ==
Les Pages Jèrriaises, commissioned by [[Société Jersiaise|La Société Jersiaise]], were initially created by Geraint Jennings, and had achieved media notice by 1996.<ref>''Jersey Evening Post'' 2/12/1996</ref> In 1999, a local contest was created to celebrate the addition of the 1,000th page.<ref>''Jersey Evening Post'' 20/8/1999</ref>
